references.citation: Wagner PD, Saltzman HA, West JB. Measurement of continuous distributions of ventilation-perfusion ratios: theory. J Appl Physiol. 1974;36(5):588-599.
references.role: Primary methodological basis for representing the lung as a distribution of V/Q units rather than one homogeneous alveolus. OpenHumSim uses six reduced compartments; it does not perform MIGET inversion.

references.citation: Wagner PD et al. Continuous distributions of ventilation-perfusion ratios in normal subjects breathing air and 100% O2. J Clin Invest. 1974.
references.role: Primary healthy-human evidence for non-zero V/Q heterogeneity and small true-shunt fractions.

references.citation: Warren GL, Cureton KJ, Middendorf WF, Ray CA, Warren JA. Red blood cell pulmonary capillary transit time during exercise in athletes. Med Sci Sports Exerc. 1991.
references.role: Primary human exercise benchmark for pulmonary capillary transit time and widening of the alveolar-arterial O2 gradient. The cohort consisted of endurance athletes, so PaO2=85 mmHg is not imposed as a universal healthy-human target.

references.citation: Torre-Bueno JR et al. Diffusion limitation in normal humans during exercise at sea level and simulated altitude. J Appl Physiol. 1985.
references.role: Primary human evidence that V/Q inequality, diffusion resistance and shunt can be separated as contributors to arterial oxygenation.

model_scope.dead_space_diagnostic: Enghoff-like diagnostic plus reduced high-V/Q wasted ventilation
not_implemented: dynamic pulmonary vascular resistance per compartment
